subject: Sector9 — Hosted inference latency commitment draft
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane@sector9.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sector9 — Hosted inference latency commitment draft

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the conversation last week. Attached is a first pass at a latency SLO proposal for Sector9's hosted inference use (PDF + a mutual action plan). High level summary below so it's easy to scan: 

- Proposed SLOs (global, US region by default):
  - p50: 80 ms (all requests)
  - p95: 320 ms (all requests)

- Measurement and windows:
  - Rolling 24-hour measurement for operational reporting; contractual measurement uses daily aggregation with a 30-day rolling window for crediting.
  - We propose per-route reporting (you can pin a route for tighter commitments) and an optional daypart carveout for predictable nightly batch peaks.

- Exceptions and carveouts:
  - Cold-starts (first request to a model shard after scale-up) are excluded from SLO measurement for a 60-second warm-up window per shard.
  - Scheduled maintenance windows (published 72 hours in advance) are excluded if >5% capacity is offline.
  - Large payload and batch inference requests flagged as background jobs are considered separately and quoted as uncached throughput commitments.

- Fallbacks and availability behavior:
  - We include an automatic soft-fallback policy: if the primary model variant exceeds p95 for two consecutive 10-minute buckets, traffic routes to a slightly smaller quantized variant we maintain for Sector9.
  - We propose a 30-day canary for the primary model serving profile before formal SLA start date.

Next steps I suggest: you and legal review the attached PDF and MAP, then we move to a short technical call to finalize per-route commitments (especially the payment-processing route you mentioned). If that looks good I'll generate a DocuSign envelope with the terms.

Attachments: SLO-draft-sector9-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan-sector9.xlsx

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Jane Park <jane@sector9.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sector9 — Hosted inference latency commitment draft

Sofia —

Appreciate the quick turn. A few immediate questions/concerns from our side:

1) Payment-processing route: we need a stricter p95 for this route (it carries synchronous authorizations). Can you propose a per-route carveout where payment-processing p95 <= 200 ms?

2) Burst behaviour: during business-hours spikes our traffic can jump 4–5x for short windows. How will the p95 measurement treat short, high-traffic bursts? We need clarity on whether short transient spikes create credit exposure.

3) Credits: outline the credit metric you propose for missed SLOs and the maximum monthly cap.

4) Evidence package: before legal proceeds we'd like the evidence bundle you can provide (historical p50/p95 samples for a representative workload, KV cache hit-rate impact summary).

We can do the technical call tomorrow afternoon — I'll bring our head of platform and legal.

—Jane Park
SVP, Engineering | Sector9
jane@sector9.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane@sector9.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sector9 — Hosted inference latency commitment draft

Hi Jane —

Quick technical clarifications and a pragmatic option that might map to your payment route needs: 

- Measurement for short bursts: our rolling 24-hour and daily aggregation logic already uses bucketed percentiles (10-minute buckets, then weighted aggregation) so short transient spikes are visible but do not automatically translate one-to-one into a daily p95 unless sustained. For contractual crediting we use a 30-day rolling window to avoid one-off spike noise.

- Per-route guarantees: we can absolutely offer a per-route p95 target for the payment-processing path. Two options:
  A) Hard per-route p95 <= 200 ms for requests that meet a defined payload/seq-length profile (higher price tier);
  B) Soft per-route target where we commit to p95 <= 280 ms with automated scaling guarantees and a guaranteed remediation SLA (faster response + incident credits) if we miss by >30% for two consecutive business-days.

- Cached vs uncached: realistic delivered latency is heavily dependent on KV cache hit-rate. We can provide a 'cached-p95' commitment (example: cached p95 <= 280 ms) and a separate 'cold/uncached' profile (uncached p95 <= 600 ms) with engineering workstreams to move more of your steady-state traffic into cached paths.

- Credits: standard template is tiered credits based on percent of affected requests aggregated monthly, capped at 10% of that month's invoice. We can discuss adjusting that cap.

I've attached our SLO evidence bundle (anonymized histograms, daypart breakdowns, and KV cache sensitivity tests).

If you'd like, Sofia can schedule a 30-minute technical call with us at 3pm PT tomorrow — we can walk the per-route definitions and map to your traffic patterns.

Attachments: slo-evidence-bundle.zip

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Jane Park <jane@sector9.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sector9 — Hosted inference latency commitment draft

Sofia/Karthik —

Thanks — that addresses most of our immediate questions. We prefer option A for the payment-processing route (hard p95 <= 200 ms) and are open to the cached/uncached split for other routes. Please flag that payment-processing will be exclusively in us-east for now.

Legal asked for a DocuSign envelope once the per-route clause is inserted; I reviewed the MAP and it looks fine. Please include the credit cap language and a 30-day canary starting on signature date.

You have approval from engineering and legal to proceed; send the DocuSign link and I'll route for signature. HubSpot deal id: S9-202706-ENT-001.

Jane Park
SVP, Engineering | Sector9
